samples.summary: Spreading one argument per table row into `Math.max` can throw `RangeError` on a pathologically large table (client-side DoS)
samples.evidence: `Math.max(0, ...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)) - 1` spreads one argument per row. V8 throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` for spreads of roughly >1e5 elements, so a document containing a table with ~100k+ rows (reachable for anyone with editor access to a shared doc, or via a crafted CRDT payload) makes `visitCellRectangleSlices` throw. Because this runs on the *read* path — `visitStyledRunsInRange` → `getRangeStyleSummary`, which the toolbar calls during React render (`text-format-group.tsx:96`) — the throw escapes into render whenever a cell rectangle is selected, breaking the toolbar for every viewer of that document rather than just the author. The old code (`editor.ts` `applyStyleToCellRange`, now deleted) had no such spread; it used `rows[r]?.cells[c]` bounds guards only. A simple `rows.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.cells.length), 0)` keeps the intended clamp with no argument-count limit.

samples.summary: The read path now descends into every cell of every table caught in a selection, amplifying per-render work on large documents
samples.evidence: `visitRangeSlices`'s top-level branch covers a table caught inside a cross-block selection "whole", iterating every block of every cell (lines 211-219). Since `getRangeStyleSummary` is invoked synchronously during toolbar render (`packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:96`, `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:426`, `mobile-toolbar.tsx:229`), a select-all over a document with a large table (e.g. 500x20 = 10k cell blocks) now walks those blocks on every re-render, where the previous read path skipped table blocks entirely (they carry no `inlines`). This is an amplification factor a hostile collaborator controls via table size; it degrades interactivity rather than granting any access, so it is hardening only. Bounding the read (early-exit once every tracked key is already 'mixed') would remove the amplification without changing the verdict.

finding.summary: New mutating model method `Doc.applyInlineStyleToCells` is outside the view-only (read-only) enforcement boundary, which is an API-level allowlist bypassed by the still-exposed `getDoc()`
finding.evidence: The docs editor enforces view-only mode by overwriting an allowlist of mutating methods on the returned `EditorAPI` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3673-3690, `MUTATING_METHODS` = applyStyle, clearInlineFormatting, insertTable, …) with no-ops, with the comment "Keep this allowlist in sync when adding mutating methods." That allowlist is not the only reachable write path: `api.getDoc()` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2650) and `api.getStore()` (2651) hand out the raw `Doc`/`DocStore`, and neither is neutralized in read-only mode. This change adds one more write primitive to that surface — `Doc.applyInlineStyleToCells` (document.ts:373) — so a holder of the api on a viewer share link can call `api.getDoc().applyInlineStyleToCells({blockId, start, end}, {bold:true})` (or `applyInlineStyle`) and mutate the shared document locally; with a Yorkie-backed store those ops propagate. Server-side enforcement exists (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts, viewer role denied `rw` at line 200) but is gated behind `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` and runs in shadow-allow mode otherwise (lines 86-105), so in a default deployment the client-side gate is the only barrier. The vector predates this diff (`applyInlineStyle` was already reachable the same way); the diff widens it by one primitive and does not extend the boundary to `getDoc()`/`getStore()`.

verdict.reason: The code exists roughly as described (document.ts:373 adds a mutating primitive; editor.ts:3641-3659 is a client-side allowlist that does not cover editor.ts:2635-2636 getDoc()/getStore()), but it is not a blocking security defect under the authorization lane. The allowlist neutralizes methods on an object that lives entirely inside the browser of the principal it purports to restrict (a viewer-share-link holder), who fully controls that runtime and can reach YorkieDocStore or the Yorkie SDK directly regardless; extending the allowlist to getDoc()/getStore() would grant zero additional protection, so no privilege boundary is crossed by adding one more model-level write primitive. The code and tests explicitly document this as a non-authoritative convenience (editor.ts:3634-3640; editor-read-only.test.ts:276-282 "getDoc() still hands out the raw model by design"), and the enforced boundary is server-side and present in code (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200 denies rw to non-editor share links). The residual concern the finding leans on — shadow-allow when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE is unset (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-87, 97-105; documented staged rollout in docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:201-204) — is a deployment-posture issue that the proposed client-side fix cannot close and is independent of applyInlineStyleToCells. This is minor hardening at most, not a major access-control defect.
